focus: The ranked edit list: 25 rows, each naming the target sk-code Rust part, the change and the rust-anything source line
noveltyJustification: The 25 rows are a ranking of findings already recorded in iterations 1-5, so they are partially new: the ranking and the target-section mapping are new, the underlying evidence is not.
keyQuestions: For each finding, does the existing sk-code Rust set under .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/ and assets/checklists/rust-checklist/ cover it, contradict it or lack it, by file and section, and what does an app-style Rust project such as a CLI or a ratatui terminal screen need that the set lacks?

label: Rank 1 scope the typed-error rule: docs-errors-and-async.md section Typed Core Errors (line 126) gains a scope clause so a generated or scaffolded port module may use anyhow or Result<T, String> internally provided the exported function maps to the typed error.
Rank 2 add the cheat guard to p1-required.md section Complete Rust Quality Gate (line 158): literals, tests and recording checks, with // recorded-literal: <reason> as the escape.

Rank 3 add the refused verdict to determinism-and-parity.md section Acceptance Standard (line 36): a function whose types cannot be faithfully bridged stays in the original language with the reason recorded.

Rank 4 add an executable source-type mapping table to overview-and-boundary-template.md section 2 (line 59), with the serde_json::Value fallback, the Option<T> default rule and a test that reads the document and checks every row.
Rank 5 add the C ABI value mapping to interop-model.md section 2 (line 35): the std::ffi width-and-sign table, the pointer-by-neighbour rule and the two refusal wordings.
Rank 6 add the operating contract and the two stop gates to SKILL.md section 4 SURFACE STANDARDS (line 125).
Rank 7 add the single-crate [lints.rust]/[lints.clippy] block and the env!("CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION") single-source pattern to build-and-organization.md section Edition, Toolchain, and MSRV (line 36).
Rank 8 add a single-crate lib+bin layout to build-and-organization.md section Workspace Layout (line 228), beside the existing five-crate workspace.

Rank 9 add the serde parity settings and attribute convention to determinism-and-parity.md section Serialized Output (line 190): float_roundtrip, preserve_order, unbounded_depth, rename_all, skip_serializing_if, serde(default) and deny_unknown_fields.
Rank 10 add the tests/fixtures tree and the trycmd CLI case format to build-and-organization.md section Testing Layout (line 136).
Rank 11 add a new cli-and-app-shape.md reference covering clap derive conventions, the exit-code contract, the stdout/stderr split, is_terminal/NO_COLOR and progress reporting.

Rank 12 add the // INFALLIBLE: <why> escape and the 3x-plus-50 size budget to p1-required.md section Complete Rust Quality Gate (line 158), scoping the unwrap/expect/panic denial to where the original returns an error.
Rank 13 add recording freshness and the committed replay report to determinism-and-parity.md section Required Parity Test Inventory (line 238).
Rank 14 add the bench-before-ship rule to build-and-organization.md section Benchmarking (line 214), noting that speed is not correctness so the timing is a separate gate.
Rank 15 add keep-the-original-shape to naming-ordering-and-signatures.md: a port keeps the original units, names and public API, and design changes wait until after the port matches.
Rank 16 add the status-doc update to build-and-organization.md section Required Verification (line 119): a change that alters observable behaviour updates the status document in the same change.

Rank 17 add the float-tolerance rule to determinism-and-parity.md section Numeric Contracts (line 51): a tolerance forgives rounding only, never formatting, and widening it to hide a mismatch is a bug in the port.
Rank 18 add prove-the-check-can-fail and the fixture-staleness rule to determinism-and-parity.md section Required Parity Test Inventory (line 238).

Rank 19 add the shadow-mode staged rollout to determinism-and-parity.md section Acceptance Standard (line 36): a port may ship returning the original result and never letting a Rust error reach a caller before it is switched on.

Rank 20 add the per-source-language trap list to determinism-and-parity.md section Numeric Contracts (line 51): UTF-16 vs UTF-8 offsets, is_alphanumeric vs isLetterOrDigit vs isalpha, int-vs-float round-tripping and the regex ASCII trap.

Rank 21 add the stall detector to build-and-organization.md section Testing Layout (line 136): three consecutive edits with no newly matching case means stop editing and surface the remaining mismatches.
Rank 22 add the port-rules file to build-and-organization.md section Testing Layout (line 136): a correction the user makes during a port is committed as one bullet and read before the next unit.
Rank 23 add the session map and claim protocol to build-and-organization.md section Testing Layout (line 136): per-unit state of open, claimed by a session and date, or done, claimed before starting.

Rank 24 add the design-tree interview to build-and-organization.md section Testing Layout (line 136): a whole-app port opens with a design-tree interview asked in rounds, each question numbered with a recommended answer.

Rank 25 name the out-of-source gaps: terminal rendering (ratatui, crossterm), signal handling, is_terminal/NO_COLOR and progress reporting are absent from both surfaces, so the edit must be sourced from the ratatui and crossterm documentation rather than from a rust-anything line.
